subject: maths

concepts.title: Empty Relation
concepts.definition: A relation on a set where no element is associated or paired with any element of the set, including itself.
concepts.key_idea: The relation contains zero ordered pairs.
question_patterns: show that the relation is empty
prove that no elements are related under the given condition
verify if the relation is an empty relation
is the relation empty
Explain the method of Empty Relation.

solution_steps.action: Identify the set and the relation condition
solution_steps.explain: Write down the set elements and the condition defining the relation.
Verify that no pair of elements from the set satisfies the given condition.
Since no ordered pairs satisfy the condition, the relation is empty.

concepts.title: Universal Relation
concepts.definition: A relation on a set where every single element is associated with every element of the set.
concepts.key_idea: The relation contains all possible ordered pairs of the Cartesian product.
question_patterns: show that the relation is universal
prove that every element is related to every other element
verify if the relation is a universal relation
is the relation universal
Explain the method of Universal Relation.

solution_steps.action: Identify the set and the relation condition
solution_steps.explain: Determine the set A and the rule that defines the relation R.

solution_steps.action: Verify the condition for all pairs
solution_steps.explain: Check if every ordered pair (a, b) in A x A satisfies the given condition.
Since all possible pairs satisfy the condition, R is equal to A x A.

concepts.title: Reflexive Relation
concepts.definition: A relation on a set where every element is related to itself.
concepts.formula: (a, a) in R for all a in A
concepts.key_idea: Each element must pair with itself for the relation to be reflexive.
question_patterns: show that the relation is reflexive
check if the relation is reflexive
prove reflexivity of the relation
is the relation reflexive
Explain the method of Reflexive Relation.

solution_steps.explain: Let a be any element belonging to the set A.

solution_steps.action: Test the relation condition for (a, a)
solution_steps.explain: Substitute a for both elements in the relation's defining rule.
If the condition holds true for all a, the relation is reflexive.

concepts.title: Symmetric Relation
concepts.definition: A relation where if one element is related to a second element, then the second element is also related to the first.
concepts.formula: (a, b) in R implies (b, a) in R
concepts.key_idea: The order of elements in the relation does not affect their relatedness.
question_patterns: show that the relation is symmetric
check if the relation is symmetric
prove symmetry of the relation
is the relation symmetric
Explain the method of Symmetric Relation.

solution_steps.action: Assume (a, b) belongs to the relation
solution_steps.explain: Assume that a is related to b under the given relation R.
Use the algebraic or logical definition to see if b is related to a.
If (b, a) is always in R whenever (a, b) is in R, the relation is symmetric.

concepts.title: Transitive Relation
concepts.definition: A relation where if a first element is related to a second, and the second is related to a third, then the first element is related to the third.
concepts.formula: (a, b) in R and (b, c) in R implies (a, c) in R
concepts.key_idea: Relatedness carries over through intermediate elements.
question_patterns: show that the relation is transitive
check if the relation is transitive
prove transitivity of the relation
is the relation transitive
Explain the method of Transitive Relation.

solution_steps.action: Assume (a, b) and (b, c) belong to the relation
solution_steps.explain: Assume both a R b and b R c are true.

solution_steps.action: Deduce the relationship between a and c
solution_steps.explain: Combine the two assumptions to show that a R c must also hold.
If (a, c) is in R for all such pairs, the relation is transitive.

concepts.title: Equivalence Relation
concepts.definition: A relation on a set that is simultaneously reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
concepts.formula: reflexive and symmetric and transitive = true
concepts.key_idea: An equivalence relation groups elements that share a common property.
question_patterns: show that the relation is an equivalence relation
prove that the relation is an equivalence relation
verify if the relation is an equivalence relation
is the relation an equivalence relation
Explain the method of Equivalence Relation.

solution_steps.explain: Show that (a, a) belongs to R for every element a in the set.
Show that if (a, b) is in R, then (b, a) is also in R.
Show that if (a, b) is in R and (b, c) is in R, then (a, c) is in R.
Since all three properties are satisfied, the relation is an equivalence relation.

concepts.title: Equivalence Class
concepts.definition: The subset of all elements in a set that are related to a specific element under an equivalence relation.
concepts.key_idea: Equivalence classes partition the set into mutually disjoint subsets.
question_patterns: find the equivalence class of
determine the set of elements related to
find the equivalence class containing
what is the equivalence class of
Explain the method of Equivalence Class.

solution_steps.explain: Identify the element a for which the equivalence class is to be found.
Set up the relation condition between an arbitrary element x and the reference element a.
Find all elements x in the set that satisfy this condition to form the equivalence class [a].

concepts.title: One-One (Injective) Function
concepts.definition: A function where distinct elements in the domain map to distinct elements in the codomain.
concepts.key_idea: No two different inputs produce the same output.
question_patterns: show that the function is one-one
prove that the function is injective
check the injectivity of the function
is the function one-one
Explain the method of One-One (Injective) Function.

solution_steps.explain: Assume f(x1) = f(x2) for two arbitrary elements x1 and x2 in the domain.
Simplify the equation f(x1) = f(x2) algebraically.
If this simplification uniquely leads to x1 = x2, the function is one-one.

concepts.title: Onto (Surjective) Function
concepts.definition: A function where every element in the codomain has at least one pre-image in the domain.
concepts.key_idea: The entire codomain is covered by the range of the function.
question_patterns: show that the function is onto
prove that the function is surjective
check the surjectivity of the function
is the function onto
Explain the method of Onto (Surjective) Function.

solution_steps.action: Set up the equation y = f(x)
solution_steps.explain: Let y be an arbitrary element in the codomain and set it equal to f(x).

solution_steps.action: Express x in terms of y
solution_steps.explain: Solve the equation for x to find the pre-image.
Check if the resulting expression for x always belongs to the domain for any y in the codomain.

concepts.title: Bijective Function
concepts.definition: A function that is both one-one (injective) and onto (surjective).
concepts.key_idea: A perfect one-to-one correspondence between the domain and codomain.
question_patterns: show that the function is bijective
prove that the function is one-one and onto
check if the function is bijective
is the function bijective
Explain the method of Bijective Function.

solution_steps.explain: Show that f(x1) = f(x2) implies x1 = x2.
Show that for every y in the codomain, there exists an x in the domain such that f(x) = y.
Since the function is both injective and surjective, it is bijective.

concepts.title: Composition of Functions
concepts.definition: The combining of two functions where the output of the first function becomes the input of the second function.
concepts.key_idea: Applying one function after another in a sequential chain.
question_patterns: find gof
find fog
calculate the composition of functions
find the composite function
Explain the method of Composition of Functions.

solution_steps.action: Write the expression for the outer function
solution_steps.explain: Identify the outer function and write its definition with the inner function as its argument.
Replace the argument of the outer function with the explicit formula of the inner function.
Perform algebraic simplification to obtain the final composite function.

concepts.title: Inverse of a Linear Function
concepts.definition: The function that reverses the operation of a linear function f(x) = ax + b, mapping the output back to the input.
concepts.key_idea: Solving for the independent variable in terms of the dependent variable.
question_patterns: find the inverse of the function
calculate the inverse function value
what is the inverse of the linear function
find the value of the inverse function at
Explain the method of Inverse of a Linear Function.

solution_steps.action: Subtract the intercept from the target value
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the constant intercept from the given y value.
Divide the difference by the slope coefficient to find the pre-image value.

solution_steps.action: Verify by substituting back into the original function
solution_steps.explain: Substitute inverse_val into f(x) = slope * x + intercept to confirm it equals y_val, ensuring the inverse is correct.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Let f(x) = {slope}x + {intercept}. Find the value of the inverse function at y = {y_val}.

extracted_variables.slope: The coefficient of x in the linear function
extracted_variables.intercept: The constant term in the linear function
extracted_variables.y_val: The value at which the inverse function is evaluated
